It sounds exhausting to carry the weight of such high expectations in a demanding environment like grad school. It is very common for high achievers to feel overwhelmed when the workload increases. Your meticulous attention to detail—while a great strength—might be exactly what makes your work take longer than your peers'. Comparing your pace to others can add unnecessary stress, which ironically makes it even harder to concentrate.

To help with your attention, try breaking your work into smaller chunks using a timer, like focusing for 25 minutes followed by a short break. This can make daunting tasks feel less overwhelming. Additionally, it could be helpful to practice setting boundaries on your perfectionism by asking yourself if a task needs to be perfect or just "good enough." Remember to be kind to yourself; grad school is a marathon, and it is okay to adjust your pace and prioritize your well-being over meeting everyone else's expectations.
